## Important comparability caveat

The FY2022 and FY2024 figures are **not directly comparable as originally reported**. General Electric underwent two spin-offs during this window:

- GE HealthCare separated January 3, 2023, and GE Vernova separated April 2, 2024; "GE's continuing operations following the GE Vernova separation, and following the earlier GE HealthCare separation, are referred to as GE Aerospace. Results of both GE HealthCare and GE Vernova are reported as discontinued operations for all periods presented" [ge_fy2024_notes.txt].

This means the same fiscal 2022 period carries three different revenue figures depending on the filing:

| FY2022 revenue basis | Amount | Source |
|---|---|---|
| As originally reported (GE incl. HealthCare + Vernova) | $76,555M | [ge_fy2022_10k.txt] |
| Recast in FY2023 10-K (ex-HealthCare, incl. Vernova) | $58,100M | [ge_fy2023_10k.txt] |
| Recast in FY2024 10-K (GE Aerospace continuing ops only) | $29,139M | [ge_fy2024_income_statement.txt] |

FY2024 GE Aerospace revenue was $38,702M [ge_fy2024_income_statement.txt].

## Calculation

The only apples-to-apples comparison is the GE Aerospace continuing-operations basis, both drawn from the FY2024 10-K:

- $38,702M ÷ $29,139M − 1 = **+32.8%** over two years (≈15.2% CAGR)

Naively comparing FY2024 ($38,702M) to GE's as-reported FY2022 ($76,555M) would show a ~49% *decline*, but that reflects the divestiture of HealthCare and Vernova, not operating performance, and should not be used.

ANSWER: On a comparable continuing-operations (GE Aerospace) basis, revenue grew ~32.8%, from $29,139M in FY2022 to $38,702M in FY2024 (~15.2% CAGR). Note this is not comparable to GE's originally reported FY2022 revenue of $76,555M, which included the since-spun-off HealthCare and Vernova businesses.
